T: Hide and clap. Then come to dinner.
D: Paranormal investigators help a family terrorised by a dark presence in their Rhode Island farmhouse.
P: Serve the mains when the Warrens arrive at the Perron farmhouse.
S: the farmhouse is in Rhode Island
Chopped clams folded into a batter of flour, baking powder, egg and clam juice, spooned into 180C oil, fried until puffed and golden. Lemon and tartare.
Fine cornmeal scalded with boiling water and salt, loosened with milk, cooked in butter on a griddle until crisp at the edges, with butter and maple.
Music box raspberry jam drop shortbread
the little music box that plays by itself

Buttery vanilla shortbread rounds with a thumbprint of raspberry jam baked in the middle, dusted with icing sugar and kept in a tin. Beat 200g soft butter with 100g caster sugar and 1 tsp vanilla until pale. Mix in 250g plain flour and 50g cornflour to a soft dough. Roll into 20 balls, flatten slightly on lined trays and press a hollow in each with your thumb. Fill each with half a teaspoon of raspberry jam. Bake at 170C for 15 to 18 minutes until pale golden at the edges, cool on the tray and dust with icing sugar.
M: dinner for a family of seven in 1971

Beef chuck seared dark and braised for hours with onion, carrot, celery and red wine, carved thick with potatoes, the braising gravy spooned over. Heat the oven to 160C. Season a 1.5kg beef chuck roast and sear hard on all sides in a heavy pot. Add 2 onions in wedges, 4 carrots and 2 celery sticks in chunks and 2 garlic cloves. Pour in 250ml red wine and 500ml beef stock, add thyme and 2 bay leaves, cover and braise for 3 hours. Add 800g halved potatoes for the last hour. Lift out the meat and veg, reduce the liquid by a third and season for gravy.
the Warrens on the road investigating
Cod baked at 200C for 15 minutes under buttery cracker crumbs with lemon and parsley, buttered peas and boiled potatoes.
W: Apples sliced and tossed with cinnamon, sugar and lemon, covered with a crumble of oats, flour, brown sugar and cold butter rubbed together, baked at 180C for 40 minutes until bubbling. Pouring cream.
K: Homemade coffee syrup blended thick with cold milk and vanilla ice cream, the way Rhode Islanders do a shake, with whipped cream and grated chocolate. Simmer 250ml strong brewed coffee with 150g caster sugar for 10 minutes until syrupy, then cool completely. Blend 120ml of the syrup with 500ml cold full cream milk and 8 big scoops of vanilla ice cream until thick and smooth. Pour into 4 tall chilled glasses, top with whipped cream and grate a little dark chocolate over each.

s.note: the farmhouse is in Rhode Island
s.how: Drain a tin of chopped clams, keeping the juice. Mix 200g flour, 2 tsp baking powder, 1 egg and 150ml clam juice and fold in the clams. Spoon into 180C oil and fry until puffed and golden. Serve with lemon and tartare.

Pour 300ml boiling water over 200g fine cornmeal and a pinch of salt and stir. Loosen with 100ml milk. Cook spoonfuls in butter on a griddle until crisp at the edges. Serve with butter and maple syrup.

m.note: the Warrens on the road investigating
m.how: Lay 4 cod fillets in a dish. Crush 100g crackers with 60g melted butter, lemon zest and parsley and press on top. Bake at 200C for 15 minutes. Serve with 800g boiled potatoes and 300g buttered peas.

w.how: Toss 6 sliced apples with 1 tsp cinnamon, 60g sugar and lemon juice in a dish. Rub 100g cold butter into 80g flour, 80g oats and 80g brown sugar. Scatter over and bake at 180C for 40 minutes. Serve with pouring cream.

d.how: Simmer 250ml strong brewed coffee with 150g caster sugar for 10 minutes until syrupy, then cool completely. Blend 120ml of the syrup with 500ml cold full cream milk and 8 big scoops of vanilla ice cream until thick and smooth. Pour into 4 tall chilled glasses, top with whipped cream and grate a little dark chocolate over each.
